problem:
The hyperbola $\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{25}=1$ intersects the line $x=-3$ at

$($
{{field-1}}, 
{{field-2}} $).$
worked_solution:
To find the points where the hyperbola intersects the line $x=-3,$ we substitute $x=-3$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{25} & =1 \\ \frac{(-3)^{2}}{9}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{25} & =1 \\ 1-\frac{{y}^{2}}{25} & =1 \\ -{y}^{2} & =0 \\ y & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the hyperbola intersects the horizontal line $x=-3$ at $(-3,0).$
